dedupe_keys.name: urban haiti optimising soil container based sanitation collection routes with datakind

description: This case study describes how the data science non-profit DataKind helped Sustainable Organic Integrated Livelihoods (SOIL), a Haitian research and development organisation, plan the routes of its waste collection fleet. SOIL provides container-based ecological sanitation toilets to more than 1,000 households a week in urban Haiti, collects the waste and turns it into compost. Its mixed fleet of vehicles faces varied road conditions, which makes routing hard. Building on a submission to Bloomberg's 2019 Data for Good Exchange, Michael Dowd, Anna Dixon and Benjamin Kinsella show how open tools, OpenStreetMap road data and Google OR-Tools, can solve this mixed-fleet vehicle routing problem. The six-page paper was posted on arXiv in October 2020 and is free to read online. Coverage is SOIL's service area in urban Haiti. Caveats: results are described as preliminary, and the household location data are not published. The authors report that SOIL was able to improve its collection routes to account for different road conditions and vehicle types, reducing operating costs and fuel use, which they describe as essential for the service's planned expansion. Simulation uses: an example of low-cost routing for sanitation and waste collection services in low-income cities. Related records: the Bahía Blanca routing instances (data-bahia-blanca-waste-collection-routing-instances) and the Liberia national EMS study (case_study-liberia-national-ems-first-22-months) show other service planning in resource-limited settings.
